chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Isma'il ibn Hammam al-Kindi from al-Rida (peace be upon him): In the case of a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth,
he said: 'The portion is one of seven. He says: "It has seven doors; for each of them [the heirs] is a portion assigned."'

key_terms.أَبْوَابٍ: Doors (metaphor for categories or paths of distribution)

ai.seo_question: How is an ambiguous bequest of 'a portion' of wealth distributed in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal interpretation of an ambiguous bequest (*al-wasiyya al-mubhama*) where the beneficiary is described vaguely. He establishes that such a bequest is fixed at one-seventh of the estate, distributed among seven distinct categories or individuals, each receiving a specific assigned share. This ruling provides practical certainty for estate distribution in cases of unclear testamentary instructions, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving ambiguity in favor of equitable division.
